title: Intertwiner coefficient system 𝒞_{x,F} = Hom(κ_x, κ_F)_{J ∩ J} (geometrization of (E4))
body_html:
Intertwiner coefficient system $\mathscr{R}_{x, \mathcal{F}}$

Theorem (Sheaf7 §8). For any point $x \in \mathcal{B}(M)$, the assignment $$\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathscr{R}_{x, \mathcal{F}} := > \Hom(\kappa_x, \kappa_\mathcal{F})_{J_x \cap J_\mathcal{F}} > \;\cong\; (\kappa_x^* \otimes \kappa_\mathcal{F})_{J_x \cap J_\mathcal{F}}$$ with the natural transition maps $r_{x, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}}$ defines a constant coefficient system of $R$-modules on $\mathcal{B}(M)$.

The constancy comes from (E4): each $\mathscr{R}_{x, \mathcal{F}}$ is one-dimensional and the transition maps $r_{x, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}}$ are isomorphisms.

We fix once and for all an isomorphism $$c_x : R \;\xrightarrow{\cong}\; \Gamma(\mathcal{B}(M), \mathscr{R}_x),$$ which by composition with restriction to $\mathcal{F}$ gives $c_x : R \cong \Hom_{J_x \cap J_\mathcal{F}}(\kappa_x, \kappa_\mathcal{F})$.

The element $c_x$ controls how the $\Res$ functor of Res and Sat functors between Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) and Coeff_M⁰(B(M)) compares $\kappa_x$ and $\kappa_\mathcal{F}$.
